gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a rule on pushchairs. The site is a mix of tarmac roads and grass, and it’s up to a kilometre from the main car park, so I would bring one with big wheels.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: No dogs or other pets anywhere on site, including the car parks. Assistance dogs and guide dogs are welcome.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You can bring your own food and drink, but glass bottles, glasses and cans aren’t allowed, and nor are BBQs. Nothing I read bans alcohol as such, so if you bring some I would decant it into plastic.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Chairs are fine and small pop up tents are allowed, but gazebos aren’t, as they block other people’s view. Poles are on the banned list too, so I would leave the windbreak at home.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I couldn’t find any refill points listed for the festival field. I would bring a full bottle in plastic, plus a flask for the early start.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There are disabled toilets right around the site, including in the disabled car park, but a Changing Places toilet isn’t mentioned. I would contact the festival before you book if you need one.

gtk.title: Carers’ tickets
gtk.text: Carer and companion tickets are booked through the Nimbus Access Card, or a free Digital Access Pass you can apply for. If someone under 16 needs a professional carer, I would contact the festival.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL. I would ask the festival before you go, and agree a meeting point in case you miss an announcement.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s no quiet or sensory space listed. The parkland is big, so I would pick a spot away from the families zone and the burners if someone needs calm.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: You can leave and come back in. Just get your hand stamped on the way out.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: I couldn’t find where the first aid point is, so I would ask a steward when you arrive. Agree a meeting point and write your phone number on younger children’s wrists.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The festival carries on, though the balloons only fly in calm air.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

Each day at Ragley feels different. Friday is an evening out with fire and fireworks. Saturday and Sunday start at dawn with the balloons and give you the long afternoon of flying. I would suggest thinking about how early your group is happy to get up, because that decides a lot.

Friday 4 June11:30 to 23:00
Saturday 5 June05:30 to 21:30
Sunday 6 June05:30 to 21:30
TicketsAdvance only
Friday, NightfireAn afternoon air display, then a balloon mass ascent in the early evening. At dusk aerobatic aircraft fly with fireworks on their wings, then up to 15 balloons fire their burners to music before a giant firework finale.
SaturdayThe gates open at 05:30 for the dawn mass ascent. Then the six hour air display, with warbirds, jets, helicopters, aerobatics and parachutists, and another chance for the balloons in the evening.
SundayThe last planned dawn mass ascent, then the air display. In 2025 there was a special shapes balloon display on the Sunday evening.

What do you most want to see?

Who’s coming?

How early can you get up?

How are you getting there?

I Would Pick The Friday

  1. WhyNightfire is something few air shows offer. You get the afternoon flying, an evening mass ascent, aircraft firing fireworks at dusk, the Fireglow and a firework finale, all without a dawn alarm.
  2. Good to knowIt finishes late, with the gates closing at 23:00. There’s some site lighting after the show, but I would bring a torch and sturdy shoes for the walk back on the grass.
  3. Getting thereThe gates open at 11:30. If you’re coming on the 247 bus, I would check the last bus time before you rely on it, as the fireworks finish late.

I Would Pick The Saturday

  1. WhyIt’s the fullest day. A dawn mass ascent, six hours of flying and another balloon chance in the evening, so if the morning is too windy you still have a second go.
  2. Good to knowIt’s a long day from 05:30, and a June dawn can be chilly. I would pack layers, and remember you can leave and come back in with a hand stamp if the children need a nap in the car.
  3. Getting thereThe 247 bus runs on a Saturday, but I would check the first bus time against the 05:30 gates. By car, I would aim to arrive about an hour before the gates.

I Would Pick The Sunday

  1. WhyYou get the last planned dawn mass ascent and a full afternoon of flying. This may work for you if Saturday is busy, or if you want the special shapes in the evening, as in 2025.
  2. Good to knowIt’s the last chance for the balloons. If the weather says no on the Sunday, there’s no next morning, so I would keep an eye on the forecast.
  3. Getting thereWhen I last checked the 247 bus had no Sunday service, so I would plan to drive or share a lift.
Jack’s tipThe balloons depend completely on the weather, so I would give yourself more than one chance. If you can, a two or three day ticket covers you. Camping is only for 3 day ticket holders, so take a look at before you book, and for when they fly.

Opening times are for 2027. Flying and balloon times haven’t been published yet, and everything in the air is weather permitting.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

Between the dawn balloons and the afternoon flying there’s a lot of day to fill, and Ragley does it well. There’s a families zone, a funfair, walkabout performers, model aircraft and plenty of stalls. The balloons have their own section, so take a look at for the Cameron Arena and the special shapes.

EntryYour festival ticket
SeatingBring your own
Meet the pilotsYes
Slipstream Enclosure£50 a day (2027)

Things To Do

Included

The Families Zone

Hands on activities, circus acts, themed crafts and little challenges for younger visitors. I think it’s a good place to let off steam while you wait for the flying.

Included

Walkabout Characters

Stilt walkers, vintage aviators and sky themed performers roam the showground. Children love to see them, so I would have the camera ready.

Rides extra

Funfair And Circus Skills

In 2026 there was a funfair and a circus skills area. Rides are mentioned again for 2027. I couldn’t find ride prices, so I would bring a little cash for them.

Included

Meet The Pilots

There’s a meet the pilots facility, and the display aircraft park up on the temporary airfield in front of the crowd line. I would go before the flying starts, while the crews have time to chat.

Included

Model Aircraft

In 2026 there were large radio controlled models, including a one third scale Yak 54, and a model warbird airfield attack with bangs and explosions. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible.

£50 a day

The Slipstream Enclosure

A seated enclosure right on the crowd line, sold as an extra ticket. This may work for you if you don’t want to carry chairs, as there’s no other seating on site.

Pay as you go

The Food Village

Street food, gourmet burgers, wood fired pizza and sweet treats. More in .

Free to browse

Stalls And Festival Merch

Gifts, aviation collectables, crafts and local makers. Official festival merch is only sold by the festival itself, so if you want a souvenir with the name on, I would look for their own stand.

How I Would Fit It In

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the crowd line first and put your chairs or a blanket down. Gazebos aren’t allowed, but a small pop up tent is.
  2. Then walk roundTake a look at the aircraft, speak to the pilots, visit the trade stalls and check the food options before the flying starts.
  3. Toilets before the displayI would go before the air display begins. If there’s a display you aren’t waiting to see, use it as a toilet break.
  4. On Friday, be back in timeOnce the evening mass ascent starts, I would stay put on the crowd line for the fireworks and the Fireglow.
Jack’s tipThe site is big parkland with very little shade. I would do the families zone and the funfair in the morning while it’s cooler, then settle in with sun cream and a picnic for the flying.

Based on the 2026 festival and what’s been announced for 2027. Entertainment and prices may change.
